2_Introduction: The current density-voltage (J-V) characteristics show that the target PSCs delivered a PCE of 18.9288%, with an elevated VOC of 1.0652 V, a JSC of 24.571 mA/cm², and an FF of 72.3233%. A 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1 precursor solution was similarly prepared using a mixture of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 6 s before the end of the program. Afterwards, the perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁, adopts a highly phase-pure, strain-minimized α-phase ABX₃ structure wherein the mixed A-site cation ensemble—comprising formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant, thermodynamically stabilizing component, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for suppressing halide vacancy formation and enhancing thermal tolerance—yields an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that suppresses δ-phase nucleation while mitigating ion migration through reduced octahedral tilting and strengthened Pb–X bonding; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) in DMF:DMSO solvent enables controlled solvation–desolvation kinetics during spin-coating—where the initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) step ensures uniform wet-film formation and interfacial wetting, followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 30 s) crystallization under dynamic shear—and the antisolvent quenching with 160 µL chlorobenzene at the critical 6 s pre-termination point selectively extracts DMSO to induce instantaneous nucleation of small, energetically favorable crystallites without premature aggregation, thereby establishing a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline scaffold with suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min drives complete solvent evaporation, promotes Ostwald ripening into large, oriented grains with low-angle grain boundaries, and facilitates Br⁻ incorporation into the iodide lattice to widen the bandgap slightly while passivating undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites at grain surfaces and interfaces—collectively yielding high crystallinity, minimal residual PbI₂ (as corroborated by absent or negligible XRD peaks at ~12.6°), narrow XRD peak FWHM indicating low microstrain and high phase purity, uniform film coverage and high grayscale intensity across optical/PL mapping images confirming morphological homogeneity and absence of voids or dewetted regions, and significantly enhanced PL intensity with prolonged biexponential decay lifetimes (>300 ns) evidencing drastic suppression of trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative channel dominance; these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic improvements synergistically enable balanced charge extraction, minimized interfacial energy loss, and reduced series resistance, culminating in a VOC of 1.0652 V, a JSC of 24.571 mA/cm², an FF of 72.3233%, and a PCE of 18.9288%.
